en.bdb: Indenticalness of the Sikh with the Guru

verses.gurmukhi: ਰਾਗ ਨਾਦ ਵਿਸਮਾਦੁ ਹੋਇ ਗੁਣ ਗਹਿਰ ਗੰਭੀਰਾ।
verses.translit_en: raag naadh visamaadh hoi gun gahir ga(n)bheeraa|

en.bdb: Elated in the music and sound (of the word), the disciple of the Guru becomes full of serene qualities.

verses.gurmukhi: ਸਬਦ ਸੁਰਤਿ ਲਿਵ ਲੀਣ ਹੋਇ ਅਨਹਦਿ ਧੁਨਿ ਧੀਰਾ।
verses.translit_en: sabadh surat liv leen hoi anahadh dhun dheeraa|

en.bdb: His consciousness gets merged into the Word and his mind stabilizes in the unstruck melody.

verses.gurmukhi: ਜੰਤ੍ਰ੍ਰੀ ਜੰਤ੍ਰ੍ਰ ਵਜਾਇਦਾ ਮਨਿ ਉਨਿਮਨਿ ਚੀਰਾ।
verses.translit_en: ja(n)trree ja(n)trr vajaidhaa man uniman cheeraa|

en.bdb: The Guru plays upon the instrument of sermon, listening to which the mind dones clothes of the highest state of equipoise (to dance before the Lord).

verses.gurmukhi: ਵਜਿ ਵਜਾਇ ਸਮਾਇ ਲੈ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦ ਵਜੀਰਾ।
verses.translit_en: vaj vajai samai lai gur sabadh vajeeraa|

en.bdb: The Sikh of the Guru, getting attuned to the instrument of teaching ultimately turns out himself to be a player of the Guru Word.
Now the omniscient Lord understands his pangs of separation.

verses.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਚੇਲਾ ਚੇਲਾ ਗੁਰੂ ਬੇਧਿ ਹੀਰੈ ਹੀਰਾ ॥੮॥
verses.translit_en: gur chelaa chelaa guroo bedh heerai heeraa ||8||

en.bdb: The disciple transforms into Guru and the guru into disciple in the same manner, as the diamond cutter in fact is also a diamond.
